correctness.rationale: For K_m□K_2 with m≥4, the exact open neighborhoods are (A\{a_i})∪{b_i} and (B\{b_i})∪{a_i}; these are 2m facets of size m. The A-side subcomplex collapses to ∂Δ(A)≃S^{m−2}, and the B-side similarly to ∂Δ(B). Their intersection is precisely the connected crown graph K_{m,m} minus the m diagonal edges: 2m vertices, m(m−1) edges, cycle rank m²−3m+1. As m−2≥2, both maps from the one-dimensional intersection to the sides are null homotopic; the homotopy pushout yields S^{m−2}∨S^{m−2}∨(m²−3m+1)S². m=4 yields 7 S², not a separately shifted degree. The original neighborhood-facet description makes the complex pure (m−1)-dimensional and the nonzero below-top H2 obstructs pure shellability. Inspected standalone verify.py, and independently computed all F2 boundary ranks at m=4,5,6 (7 S²; 11 S²+2 S³; 19 S²+2 S⁴); the all-m claim rests on the homotopy proof, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: DECISIVE EXACT PRIOR COVERAGE. A DISTINCT published indexed Resultary result titled 'Neighborhood complexes of two-row rook graphs split into two spheres and a crown suspension' (full RESULT.md read) works with R_n=L(K_{2,n})≅K_2□K_n. The graph is isomorphic to the submitted K_m□K_2 by commutativity of Cartesian product (n=m); its open Lovász neighborhood complex is exactly the same object. That complete published theorem yields precisely (∨² S^{n−2})∨(∨^{n²−3n+1} S²) for every n≥4, with identical crown graph K_{n,n}−M, null homotopy pushout proof and finite F2 Betti ranks. Submitted lower-degree H2 and purity/nonshellability are elementary corollaries of the already stated identical formula and facets. Search titles or different graph aliases cannot rescue originality. No substantive independent remainder survives in the original final claim; reject rather than repair by disclaimers.
residual_risks: The publication timestamps for the two same-day indexed records were not independently resolved; rejection is based on exact existing mathematical coverage, not asserting which record had an earlier hour.
